subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: An infant first gains control over the muscles near the centre of the body (trunk, shoulders) before gaining fine control over the muscles farther away (fingers, toes). This pattern of development, proceeding from the centre of the body outward to the extremities, is called the:
explanation: The proximodistal principle describes development proceeding from the centre (proximal) of the body outward to the extremities (distal) — complementary to the cephalocaudal principle, which describes development proceeding head-to-tail.

subject: Child Development & Pedagogy
stem: Some psychologists (like Piaget) argue that development happens in distinct, qualitatively different stages, while others argue it happens gradually and continuously without sharp breaks. This classic debate in developmental psychology is called the:
explanation: The continuity-discontinuity debate concerns whether development is a smooth, gradual process (continuous) or occurs in distinct qualitative stages (discontinuous, as stage theorists like Piaget argue) — a separate question from nature-versus-nurture, which concerns the SOURCE of development.
